title: Throughput credit bucket and fallback compensation language for Dedicated plans
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Objective: Define an operationally measurable throughput credit bucket, failure-triggered fallback compensation, and contract wording that ties dedicated capacity guarantees to autoscaling and fleet controls. The goal is a clear, auditable SLA and remediation path that balances commercial guarantees with our autoscale safety controls and supports automated credit calculation in billing.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SLA definition includes measurement window, numerator/denominator, and fallback eligibility. 2) Error budget math produces a daily/weekly credit amount expressible as billing units. 3) Contract language for credits and notice windows is draft-ready for legal review. 4) Linkage to autoscale policy: when autoscale cannot meet a pledge due to capacity constraints, fallback model and credit computation are triggered. 5) Monitoring signals and runbook snippets included for ops.
background: Customers buying Dedicated commit to a baseline throughput (tokens/sec or rps) with agreed SLOs. Historically we used ad-hoc credit calculations after incidents. This ticket establishes a repeatable bounded credit bucket (percentage of committed throughput) and a clear fallback compensation mechanism when autoscale/fleet controls prevent fulfilling the commitment. It aims to reduce disputes and speed remediation/credit issuance.
proposal_summary: 1) Measurement: 7-day rolling window measured in 1-minute buckets; committed throughput is the 95th percentile of committed throughput over the month; achieved throughput is per-minute successful served capacity (excluding mitigation fallbacks). 2) Error budget: shortfall = max(0, committed_throughput - achieved_throughput) aggregated across the window, converted to 'throughput-seconds' and then to credit units using committed rate pricing. 3) Credit bucket: customers accrue credits up to 5% of monthly committed fees (configurable per contract tier). 4) Fallback compensation: if autoscale policy triggered a graceful degradation (fallback model variant or queued requests) and the customer opted into 'aggressive guaranteed mode', automatic credits equal to computed shortfall are applied; otherwise, a partial manual review is required. 5) Fleet controls: AZ failover and region fallback are treated as distinct failure classes with separate thresholds for crediting. 6) Contract language: short notice windows (72 hours) for claiming credits, automatic issuance for high-severity failures (operator-validated), and escalation path to Customer Success and Legal.
detailed_measurement_spec: - Bucketization: 60s buckets, aligned to UTC. - Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows pre-notified (>=72h) and agreed capacity upgrades. - Aggregation: compute per-bucket shortfall, then sum for the measurement window. - Conversion: throughput-seconds shortfall * contract per-token rate -> credit amount. - Minimum credit threshold: $10 or 0.5% of monthly fees (whichever is higher).
contract_snippets: 1) SLA clause (draft): 'Redwood guarantees that Dedicated capacity will provide at least X throughput during the Measurement Window. In the event of measurable shortfall, Redwood will issue Service Credits as set out in the Throughput Credit Schedule. Credits for a calendar month are limited to the Credit Cap set forth in the Order Form.' 2) Fallback clause (draft): 'If Redwood's autoscaling or fleet-control policies initiate a documented fallback (model variant, queued requests, or regional failover) that reduces committed throughput, customer may be eligible for automatic Service Credits. Eligibility requires either: (a) enrollment in Aggressive Guaranteed Mode, or (b) a validated incident meeting High-Severity criteria as defined in Appendix A.'
ops_runbook_snippets: - Signal list: sustained per-az 1min served throughput < 80% of committed for >5 minutes; KV cache thrashing > 10% increase in miss rate; kernel OOM or GPU preemption events. - Play: page on-call, set mitigation mode, notify CS with incident id, open credit calculation ticket if incident classified as SLA-eligible. - Postmortem: publish within 7 days and attach credit calc to the incident artifact.
billing_integration_notes: - Billing will accept automated credit payloads from the SLO service. Payload fields: customer_id, month, credit_amount_usd, incident_ids (comma-separated). - Fallback automation: when automatic-credits flag is true, billing applies the credit to next invoice; otherwise it opens a review queue. - Logging: every credit event must include the computed shortfall, measurement window, and which fleet-control (if any) was responsible.
example_scenarios: 1) Regional outage: Region A lost capacity; achieved shortfall across affected buckets converts to $12k; Credit Cap is 5% of monthly fees ($20k) -> automatic credit issued. 2) Autoscale hit due to noisy neighbor: autoscale prevented additional allocations because pool exhausted; customer not in Aggressive Guaranteed Mode -> manual review required, provisional 25% credit pending ops verification. 3) Minor transient blips: aggregated shortfall < minimum credit threshold -> no credit issued, but incident recorded.
open_questions: - Should Credit Cap be tiered by committed spend or flat percent? (PM/Legal) - How to incorporate prior months' usage growth into committed baseline without over-crediting? (Billing/Finance) - Do we allow customers to purchase a higher 'hard guarantee' with financial penalties for Redwood? (Sales/Legal)
